name: Frame-0 premise block
template: One block, 1–3 short lines, plain white sans-serif with a soft shadow, centred at chest/upper-body height, on screen from frame 0, no animation, stays for the whole Reel or until the first beat
examples: The first girl you sleep with after losing the love of your life
When they actually tease instead of going straight to it
mechanism: Autoplay is muted and the thumbnail is the first frame: the text must deliver the entire premise before any audio. Centred placement stays inside the safe zone under the caption and the right-hand buttons.
anti_pattern: Text that appears at second 2; text in the bottom 20% (covered by caption) or top 10% (covered by the username); word-by-word animation; a title plus a subtitle.
observed: Every Reel over 1M in the sample used exactly this treatment

name: Quotation marks for a line someone said
template: Wrap the on-screen line in straight quotes so it reads as something said TO you; your face does the reacting
examples: "You're the only girl I talk to"
"How many times a day do you need to be cracked to keep your attitude in check?"
mechanism: The quotes turn the text into a shared experience rather than a statement; the audience replies with their own version.
anti_pattern: Quoting yourself; using quotes around a caption-style sentence.
observed: 136K and 16.7K on the same account — the sharper, more universal quote won

name: Stacked descriptor list
template: Three-plus hyper-specific descriptors in a row inside the premise ("6'5", tatted, tan, gym rat") — the list is the joke and the rewatch
examples: Me to my 🥺 when the 6'5", tatted, tan, gym rat walks into the gym
mechanism: Each descriptor is a micro-payoff; readers re-read the list, which registers as watch time and replays on a short Reel.
anti_pattern: Generic adjectives; more than five descriptors (unreadable in the first second).

name: No on-screen text (visual-first)
template: No overlay; the visual and the audio drop are the hook; caption is two words
examples: Outfit/arrival reveal on a beat drop
mechanism: Removes the reading step; relies on the audio page and the first frame's visual pull. Only recommend when the visual genuinely carries it — otherwise expect sub-follower-count reach.
anti_pattern: Using this because you didn't write a premise.
observed: Median ~0.1× followers on the visual-only account sampled; outliers are trend-timed

name: Mid-video text pop-in as pattern interrupt
template: A second, smaller text element that appears exactly at the payoff or twist (a number, a name, 'wait for it' is banned) and disappears after ~1.5 s
mechanism: A visual change at the payoff resets attention and marks the moment people rewind to; it creates the 'hump' shape in the retention curve.
anti_pattern: 'Wait for it'; constant captions-style subtitles that never change.
observed: Galloway 'hump' retention shape; not present in the sampled skit accounts, which are short enough not to need it
